title: Quantitative analysis of naphthalene and naphthols in geothermal fluids using SPE with HPLC
author: Sajkowski, Seward, et al.
materials: To isolate, enrich and increase analyte recovery, a solid phase extraction method was developed. Three different SPE cartridges were tested. Two of them with the same polymer base but different amounts of sorbent, (i.e. Discovery DSC-18 with either 100 mg and 500 mg sorbent from Sigma-Aldrich and Strata-X 33 µm Polymeric Reversed Phase, 30 mg from Phenomenex. Before using the cartridges, they were eluted with ethanol and then conditioned with water (Table 4) after which, 1 ml of sample (i.e. spiked sample) was loaded. The cartridges are dried with nitrogen gas for 5 min (20 psi and 2.0 l min−1). Subsequently, the analyte was eluted with ethanol (or methanol) and collected into a vial and analyzed with HPLC.Table 4Parameters used during evaluation of SPE protocol. The suggested optimum version has been highlighted.Table 4*as the wash solution: 30:70, v/v, ethanol/water solution was used, or: 40:60, v/v, methanol/water.**eluent used in this study: 99.9% ethanol or 100% methanol HPLC grade.

steps.title: Prepare stock calibration solution
steps.instruction: Spike HPLC‑grade ethanol with naphthalene at 7.80×10⁻⁵ mol kg⁻¹ and both 1‑naphthol and 2‑naphthol at 6.94×10⁻⁵ mol kg⁻¹ to make the stock solution for calibration standards.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Using the stock solution, prepare eight calibration solutions covering 2.9–1170 nmol kg⁻¹ (Table 3 values: 12.9, 215, 376, 441, 205, 245, 654, 878, 408, 1170 nmol kg⁻¹). Calibration solutions 1–5 are prepared stepwise: solutions 1–3 are made by diluting solution 5, while solutions 4 and 5 are prepared by diluting solution 7. Use unspiked HPLC‑grade ethanol as the blank.

steps.title: Condition SPE cartridges
steps.instruction: For each cartridge (Discovery DSC‑18 100 mg, Discovery DSC‑18 500 mg from Sigma‑Aldrich, and Strata‑X 33 µm 30 mg from Phenomenex), first elute with ethanol, then condition with water as described in Table 4.

steps.title: Load sample onto cartridge
steps.instruction: Load 1 mL of the sample (spiked or geothermal brine) onto the conditioned SPE cartridge.

steps.title: Dry cartridge with nitrogen
steps.instruction: Dry the cartridge with nitrogen gas for 5 min at 20 psi and a flow rate of 2.0 L min⁻¹.

steps.title: Wash cartridge
steps.instruction: Wash the cartridge with either a 30:70 v/v ethanol/water solution or a 40:60 v/v methanol/water solution (both used as wash solutions in the study).

steps.title: Elute analytes
steps.instruction: Elute the retained analytes with 99.9 % ethanol (or 100 % methanol, HPLC grade) and collect the eluate into a clean vial.

steps.title: Analyze eluate by HPLC
steps.instruction: Inject the collected eluate into the HPLC system; plot the quotients of the integrated peaks versus the known standard concentrations to generate linear calibration curves (R² = 0.9992–0.9998) for quantification of naphthalene, 1‑naphthol and 2‑naphthol.

steps.title: Adjust SPE for geothermal brine
steps.instruction: When processing geothermal brine (pH ≈ 5.5) spiked with 10 µg kg⁻¹ of each analyte, adjust all SPE steps (conditioning, loading, washing, elution, modifiers). Test brine samples with NaCl concentrations of 0.00, 0.05, 0.50 and 1.00 mol kg⁻¹.

steps.title: Select optimal cartridge and solvents
steps.instruction: Based on recovery tests, use the Discovery‑C18 100 mg cartridge (provides ~99–100 % recovery). Choose ethanol as the eluent (ethanol gave higher recovery than methanol) and use a 30 % ethanol solution as the wash (the highest organic concentration that does not elute the target compounds). Test solvent concentrations from 10 % to 100 % for both methanol and ethanol to confirm optimal performance.

steps.title: Minimize plastic contamination
steps.instruction: Store all samples and standards in glass bottles/vials and handle solutions with glass pipettes to avoid leaching of plastic contaminants.
